annotations.title: Review an economy as a cheater would

description: Reviews an economy the way a cheater reads it, before it goes live (a review, not a validity check). For every route that pays or gives value it says who can trigger it, what the program enforces, what it trusts off the chain, and the most one cheater gets; then findings with stable ids and a severity; then, for each grant paid on vouchers, whether its server decides, replays or only bounds the result (its "trust"), what a cheater gets at that level, and what the next level costs to build. Takes the spec inline (`spec`) or a worked example by name. Answers { ok (false when a finding is high, or the spec does not check: then `refusals`), routes: [{ kind ("grant", "farm", "item", "box", "payment", "recipe", "lottery", "contest", "auction", "schedule", "hold", "decision"), key, name, trigger, enforced: [words], trusts: [words], trust ("decides" | "replays" | "bounds" | null), ceiling (words), feeds: ["farm:<key>", …: what its prize is staked in, crafted into or buys] }], findings: [{ id (R-…), severity ("high" | "medium" | "low" | "info"), route ("grant:<key>", "farm:<key>", … or "economy"), message, fix }] }; the trade-offs are in its text.

example.description: A worked example by name (stud-farm, nft-raffle, …).

spec.description: An economy spec (version 2) given inline. Takes precedence over file and example.
